ov: 118 species of small to medium-sized, brightly coloured birds with large heads, long dagger-like bills, short legs and stubby tails. Their blues come from the structure of the feathers, which scatters blue light, not from pigment. Many live away from water and eat small invertebrates, not fish.
wt: 9–12 g (African dwarf) to almost 500 g (laughing kookaburra)
rg: Worldwide, but most species live in the tropics of Africa, Asia and Oceania.
df: Fish for some; many species take small invertebrates, swooping down from a perch.
fx: Kingfishers nest in tunnels dug into banks, and some nest inside termite mounds in trees.
The giant kingfisher digs nest tunnels up to 8.5 m long, the longest recorded.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact is confirmed by Wikipedia (500 Series Shinkansen): the train’s nose mimics a kingfisher’s beak, cutting energy use by 15%. PAGE ADDITIONS 2026-11-02 (ov, len, wt, fx), from the cached Wikipedia text.
